text:
Find Location and Auto-Plan takes an address or G P S coordinates, and shows the spot on a map and in [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/), with its ground height.
Tap Build plan for this location, and the app looks over the terrain for a good tower spot nearby, and sets up the sites for you to review.
Each survey spot and its view cones show on every flat map, and in the [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) tilt view over the satellite pictures.

Above every map, tap [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) tilt view.
The map turns into a [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) model of the ground, with satellite pictures on top.
Drag the tilt slider, or tap Straight down, Tilted, or Low angle.

Next, plot your radio path.
Type G P S coordinates or an address for point [A](/ˈA/) and point B, use your phone's G P S, or tap Pick on [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) and touch the ground.
In the [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) tilt view, every hop shows where to aim the antenna at each end, and how far to tilt it up or down.

Turn on the signal heat map to shade predicted signal around your lines.
In the [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) tilt view, the lines and the heat map show right on the ground.

Every map and [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) view can open on a full page with its own buttons.
Tap Full page above the map to open it.

Tap Tilt to see the same area in [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/).
Use the up and down arrows to tilt, and the round arrows to turn the view.
Tap [N](/ˈɛn/) to put north back at the top.

Section three is low-voltage design.
On Auto-Design, describe the building: its type, floors and size.
The app recommends the devices for each system, lays them out, and shows them on a [2D](/tˌu dˈi/) plan and a [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) model.
The page called [2D](/tˌu dˈi/) and [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) Models with Layers shows every system on the job.

The [2D](/tˌu dˈi/) plan is drawn to true scale.
Every system has its own layers: devices, coverage, cable runs and signal heat maps.
Tap Only this to see one system by itself, and tap anything to see what it is.

Switch to the [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) model to see the whole building.
Pull the floors apart to look inside, and drag to turn it.
The [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) site model shows the whole campus, with the links between the buildings.

Indoor Coverage and [DAS](/dˈæs/) lets you draw the walls, pick what they are made of, and place antennas.
The coverage shows right away, on the plan or in [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/).

Tap the [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) view button to see the beam as a green wedge over the terrain.
It stops where it meets the ground.
Tilt the view, and turn on the signal heat map.
The same true scale choice is on the path profile, the drawn line chart, the run profiles, and every [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) view.

[3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) Model shows the terrain, the towers and the [Fresnel](/fɹənˈɛl/) zone in [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/).
While you are online, the app downloads the terrain and existing towers around your sites by itself, and saves them for offline use.
